brief: A 3D-printed PLA spacer block. The base is a 40 mm by 25 mm plate 5 mm thick. A 10 mm diameter post 8 mm tall stands in the middle of it, with a 1.5 mm fillet where the post meets the plate. A 4 mm hole runs all the way through the post and the plate. Two 3 mm mounting holes pass all the way through the plate, 30 mm apart. It must weigh no more than 10 g. It carries no load - it is a printed spacer, so there is no load case.

REQ_MOUNTING_HOLE_COUNT counted `mounting` 2 as a bound; the brief states the count -- "two 3 mm mounting holes pass all the way through the plate, 30 mm apart" -- so it is exactly that many.
added REQ_MASS at_most 10 g: the brief states it as a limit and the whole-part mass slot was left empty, so nothing would have checked the one number a printed part is most often judged on
dropped `UNKNOWN_WEIGHT`: it asks what the part weighs, which is not something anyone supplies -- it is measured on the built part, against the mass requirement already in the record

added REQ_HOLES_4MM: the brief states 1 open hole of 4 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.
